lessons.title: Choosing Pronouns and Verb Forms
lessons.learn: Hindi marks respect in two places at once: the pronoun (तू, तुम, आप) and the verb that agrees with it. Choosing the right pronoun but leaving the verb in the familiar form is the most common register error at this level. Read every sentence twice: once for the pronoun, once for the verb ending.

vocab.en: respect particle added to a name or word

grammar.title: Pronoun and verb agreement
grammar.explain: आप takes plural verb forms even when one person is addressed: आप आते हैं, आप बोलिए। तुम takes the second-person familiar forms (आते हो, बोलो). तू takes the singular -ता/-ती ending (आता है). The respect of a name is carried by जी, not by the pronoun alone: गुप्ता जी, माँ जी. A respectful pronoun with a familiar verb sounds rude, and a familiar pronoun with a formal verb sounds confused.
grammar.pattern: आप + plural-agreeing verb (हैं, -िए, -ेंगे) · तुम + -ो / -ते form · तू + -ता / -ती form
mistakes: आप आता है → आप आते हैं: the verb takes plural agreement with आप even for one person.
Using तू with a stranger, an elder or an official sounds deliberately rude.
Dropping जी from a name: 'प्रकाश, आइए' is abrupt; 'प्रकाश जी, आइए' is warm.

dialogue.t: रमेश जी, आप कल की बैठक में आएँगे?
dialogue.r: Ramesh jī, āp kal kī baiṭhak mẽ āẽge?
dialogue.en: Mr Ramesh, will you attend tomorrow's meeting?

dialogue.t: हाँ, मैं आऊँगा। आप भी आइए।
dialogue.r: Hā̃, maĩ āūgā. Āp bhī āie.
dialogue.en: Yes, I will come. You should come too.

dialogue.t: आप तो हमेशा समय पर आते हैं, इसीलिए मैंने पूछा।
dialogue.r: Āp to hamesha samay par āte haĩ, isīliye maĩne pūchhā.
dialogue.en: You always arrive on time, which is why I asked.

dialogue.t: आपकी बात से बहुत हौसला मिला।
dialogue.r: Āpkī bāt se bahut hausalā milā.
dialogue.en: Your words gave me a lot of encouragement.

quiz.why: आप takes plural agreement (आते हैं) even when one listener is addressed.

lessons.title: Requests, Permission and Politeness
lessons.learn: Requests in Hindi are shaped by the verb and by a softening frame. The formal imperative (-िए) and permission questions (क्या मैं … सकता/सकती हूँ?) let you ask without commanding. Politeness at this level means choosing the frame that fits the cost of the request to the listener.

grammar.title: Softened requests
grammar.explain: Use the -िए imperative with आप (बैठिए, लिखिए). Soften with क्या मैं … सकता/सकती हूँ? for permission and क्या आप … सकते/सकती हैं? for help. The conditional frame यदि आपको कष्ट न हो, तो … lowers the cost of the request. The verb सकना agrees with the speaker's gender: सकता for a man, सकती for a woman.
grammar.pattern: क्या + मैं / आप + verb stem + सकता/सकती/सकते + हूँ/हैं ? · यदि आपको कष्ट न हो, तो + polite imperative

examples.t: क्या मैं यहाँ बैठ सकता हूँ?
examples.r: kyā maĩ yahā̃ baiṭh saktā hū̃?
examples.en: May I sit here? (said by a man)

examples.t: क्या आप मेरी सहायता कर सकती हैं?
examples.r: kyā āp merī sahāyatā kar saktī haĩ?
examples.en: Could you help me? (said to a woman)

examples.t: यदि आपको कष्ट न हो, तो एक गिलास पानी दीजिए।
examples.r: yadi āpko kaṣṭ na ho, to ek gilās pānī dījie.
examples.en: If it is no trouble, please give me a glass of water.

mistakes: Bare imperative with a stranger: 'पानी दो' sounds like an order; 'पानी दीजिए' is the courteous form.
A woman saying सकता हूँ: the verb must agree with her gender: सकती हूँ.
Asking an elder क्या तुम मदद करोगे?: use आप with the -िए or क्या आप … सकते हैं? frame.

dialogue.t: माफ़ कीजिए, क्या यह बस स्टैंड का रास्ता है?
dialogue.r: Māfa kījie, kyā yah bas sṭāṇḍ kā rāstā hai?
dialogue.en: Excuse me, is this the way to the bus stand?

dialogue.t: जी हाँ, आप सीधे चलिए और दूसरे मोड़ पर बाएँ मुड़िए।
dialogue.r: Jī hā̃, āp sīdhe calie aur dūsre moṛ par bāẽ muṛie.
dialogue.en: Yes, go straight on and turn left at the second corner.

dialogue.t: क्या मैं आपसे एक और सवाल पूछ सकता हूँ?
dialogue.r: Kyā maĩ āpse ek aur savāl pūchh saktā hū̃?
dialogue.en: May I ask you one more question?

lessons.title: Writing a Formal Letter
lessons.learn: Formal Hindi letters follow a stable frame: the addressee line, the subject line, a respectful salutation, a body written in the impersonal passive, and a formal closing. Mastery here is about frame and tone, not long sentences. Keep one register from the first line to the last.

vocab.en: to (the service of) — opening of a formal letter

grammar.title: Frame, passive and closing
grammar.explain: The body uses the impersonal passive to keep the tone objective: निवेदन किया जाता है, सूचित किया जाता है। The salutation depends on the addressee: महोदय for a man in office, महोदया for a woman, and आदरणीय with a name for a known person. Close with सादर or भवदीय, never with the informal आपका मित्र.
grammar.pattern: सेवा में, [title] · विषय: … · आदरणीय / महोदय · body in passive · सादर, [name]

examples.t: आपको सूचित किया जाता है कि परीक्षा एक सप्ताह बाद होगी।
examples.r: āpko sūcit kiyā jātā hai ki parīkṣā ek saptāh bād hogī.
examples.en: You are informed that the examination will be held a week later.

examples.t: अतः आपसे निवेदन है कि शुल्क शीघ्र जमा करें।
examples.r: ataḥ āpse nivedan hai ki śulk śīghra jamā kareṃ.
examples.en: Therefore, I request you to deposit the fee promptly.

mistakes: Closing an official letter with आपका मित्र or बाय.
Switching from आप in the body to तुम or तू: keep one register throughout.
Writing a body with no actionable request, so the reader does not know what to do.

dialogue.t: प्रधानाचार्य महोदय, आपके पत्र का उत्तर भेज दिया गया है।
dialogue.r: Pradhānācārya mahodaya, āpke patra kā uttar bhej diyā gayā hai.
dialogue.en: Sir, the reply to your letter has been sent.

dialogue.t: अच्छा। क्या विषय स्पष्ट लिखा गया था?
dialogue.r: Acchā. Kyā viṣay spaṣṭ likhā gayā thā?
dialogue.en: Good. Was the subject line written clearly?

dialogue.t: जी हाँ, विषय में परीक्षा की तिथि साफ़ लिखी है।
dialogue.r: Jī hā̃, viṣay mẽ parīkṣā kī tithi sāf likhī hai.
dialogue.en: Yes, the exam date is clearly written in the subject line.

dialogue.t: ठीक है। अंत में 'सादर' लिख दीजिए।
dialogue.r: Ṭhīk hai. Anta mẽ 'sādar' likh dījie.
dialogue.en: Fine. Please write 'sādar' at the end.

practice.q: Which closing is correct for a formal letter?
आपको सूचित किया ____ है कि बैठक कल होगी। (use the passive)
Translate into Hindi: We request you to submit the form by Friday.
practice.answer: आपसे निवेदन है कि आप शुक्रवार तक फ़ॉर्म जमा करें।

practice.q: Translate into English: आदरणीय महोदय, मैं आपका ध्यान एक समस्या की ओर खींचना चाहता हूँ।
practice.answer: Respected Sir, I want to draw your attention to a problem.

practice.q: Put the letter parts in order: सादर / विषय: छुट्टी का आवेदन / सेवा में, प्रधानाचार्य महोदय
practice.answer: सेवा में, प्रधानाचार्य महोदय — विषय: छुट्टी का आवेदन — सादर

practice.q: Correct the closing of a letter to your bank manager: 'आपका मित्र'
A: महोदय, क्या मैं अपनी छुट्टी का आवेदन भेज सकता हूँ? B: (give a formal yes)
practice.answer: जी हाँ, कृपया उसे विषय सहित भेज दीजिए।

practice.q: Match each phrase to its function.

practice.answer: आपसे निवेदन है कि कल की बैठक में अवश्य उपस्थित रहें।

practice.q: Write the opening and subject line of a leave application.
practice.answer: सेवा में, प्रधानाचार्य महोदय। विषय: दो दिन की छुट्टी का आवेदन।

quiz.q: Which salutation is right for a male official?
quiz.why: महोदय is the formal address for a man in office; महोदया is for a woman.

quiz.q: Why is the passive सूचित किया जाता है used in formal letters?
options: It keeps the tone impersonal and official
quiz.why: The passive removes the personal voice and sounds objective.

quiz.q: Which closing belongs to a formal letter?
quiz.why: भवदीय and सादर are standard formal closings.

quiz.q: What does विषय mean in a letter?
Which register mistake is most visible in a formal letter?
options: Switching to तुम in the body
quiz.why: A switch to a familiar pronoun breaks the register of the whole letter.
